_comment: Company marks for organisations A-L, licence-triaged and fetched 2026-08-22 for the published commercial build. Scope: organisations whose name begins A-L and which are actors in the history - the company where the incident happened, who shipped the fix, who published the paper, who ran the system that fell over. Bar applied: a named war story, an origin-story dateline role, or a substantive multi-sentence account of something the organisation built, broke or published. A single-clause citation, an adopter mention or a vendor list does not qualify. Every file below was licence-checked on its own Commons description page via the API's extmetadata and then against the raw wikitext template, never off the article that uses it. Every mark is reproduced unaltered - sanitised only - and is used nominatively to identify the company the history describes; it must never be placed where it reads as endorsement, partnership or sponsorship, never used as this product's own branding, favicon or OG image, and the owner is named in every credit. M-Z organisations are a separate pass and a separate manifest.

rejected.name: Kafka
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 143 times, always Apache Kafka the log. LinkedIn built and open-sourced it and carries the mark instead.

rejected.name: Cassandra
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 65 times as the wide-column store. The actors around it are Facebook (which wrote it), Discord and Netflix (which run it).

rejected.name: Redis
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 211 times and essentially never about Redis Ltd. The book's own warning case.

rejected.name: Postgres / PostgreSQL
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named ~110 times as the database. No vendor acts anywhere in the corpus.

rejected.name: MySQL
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 49 times as the database - Google's AdWords backend, GitHub's primaries. Oracle never appears as an actor.

rejected.name: DynamoDB
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 42 times as the managed store. Amazon is the actor and ships a mark.

rejected.name: Elasticsearch
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 23 times as the search engine. Elastic the company acts once, in p1c14, and is listed under fallback.

rejected.name: Flink
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 31 times as the stream processor. Alibaba is the actor and ships a mark.

rejected.name: Apache / Apache Software Foundation
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Almost always a project prefix - Apache Flink, Apache Airflow, Apache Lucene. The single ASF mention in p3c19 is a stewardship clause about where Lucene was donated, not an incident, a fix or a paper.

rejected.name: Kubernetes
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 4 times as the orchestrator; once as 'the brain of Kubernetes' describing etcd.

rejected.name: Hadoop
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 4 times as a batch destination in LinkedIn's pipeline tangle.

rejected.name: HBase
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 7 times as an LSM store and as what sat behind Facebook's ODS.

rejected.name: Lucene
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 10 times as the library. p3c19's war story is about Doug Cutting, a person, and the Apache Software Foundation.

rejected.name: etcd, ZooKeeper, Consul
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named as rentable consensus primitives; 'strip away the branding and each is the same product' is the book's own line.

rejected.name: Debezium
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Named 5 times as the standard CDC tool.

rejected.name: Storm, Spark, Samza, Airflow, Druid, ClickHouse, CockroachDB, Riak, Prometheus, Solr, Memcached, NGINX, HAProxy, Envoy, Akka, Erlang, gRPC, Protobuf, Vitess
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Each named as software in a field guide or a component list.

rejected.name: Bigtable, Spanner, Chubby, Colossus, Dynamo
rejected.reason: Not an actor, technology name only. Google and Amazon internal systems. The parent companies are the actors and both ship marks.

rejected.name: Apple
rejected.reason: Not an actor. One epilogue clause in p3c21 ('Apple republished the shape, 1 May 2009') and a protocol detail in p3c03 about the apns-expiration header. No incident, no fix, no paper of its own. File:Apple logo black.svg is additionally tagged {{PD-US-no notice}}, a contestable claim on a famous pictorial mark.

rejected.name: ABC
rejected.reason: Not an actor. A single adopter clause in p3c21: 'ABC shipped full-length HD on it, 24 July 2007.'

rejected.name: EchoStar
rejected.reason: Not an actor. A single acquisition clause in p3c21: bought Move Networks' assets on the last day of 2010. The chapter's history is Move's.

rejected.name: Ericsson
rejected.reason: Not an actor. One subordinate clause in p3c04 - 'a language Ericsson built for telephone switches' - inside a war story about WhatsApp.

rejected.name: HashiCorp
rejected.reason: Not an actor. Vendor possessive on products in p2c10: 'HashiCorp's Consul and Serf'. The sentence is about the SWIM protocol.

rejected.name: Confluent
rejected.reason: Not an actor. One clause in p2c09: 'Kreps co-founded Confluent to commercialize Kafka.' No incident, no system, no paper.

rejected.name: data Artisans / Ververica
rejected.reason: Not an actor. One clause in p2c09 recording that Alibaba acquired it. Alibaba is the actor.

rejected.name: Fastly
rejected.reason: Not an actor. Named once, inside a four-item CDN vendor list in p1c07.

rejected.name: Adyen
rejected.reason: Not an actor. Named only as the alternative PSP beside Stripe in p3c14's scoping paragraph.

rejected.name: DoorDash
rejected.reason: Not an actor at the bar used here. A single-clause citation in p3c06 that its dispatch team 'has written about exactly this'. No incident and no named war story; a mark beside one citation is soup.

rejected.name: IEEE
rejected.reason: Not an actor. A publication venue - 'IEEE Micro, 2003' - in p3c19's citation of the Google Cluster Architecture paper.

rejected.name: AFIPS
